**Prior Degrees:** Mechanical Civil Engineer

Stefano Sacco joined the Canadian Centre for Welding and Joining lab in 2021 to pursue a MSc. In Materials Engineering. Stefano is a Mechanical Civil engineer from the “Universidad de Chile” with a minor on renewable energies. He has also been involved in the UofA CWB association Student chapter as Vice-President after having served as the counsellor of the Mechanical Engineering FCFM Student Chapter 2019-20.

The project in which Stefano is working has it focus in creating a model to estimate the hydrogen concentration in the billets and rods.  The novelty about his research is that it allows to estimate the amount of hydrogen in each stage of the steelmaking, thing that no one has never been able to do before. He is also working on Plasma physics on Tungsten arc welding, and he has presented on two conferences about the it. He won the CWBA “Outstanding team member award” from his collaborations within the laboratory and different companies. Other recognitions that he has received are a full MIT scholarship to do a Machine Learning course in Boston, the Becas Santander exchange award, and the “Mechanical Engineering Honor Student Award 2020”.

Stefano enjoys playing basketball, swimming and well, doing any type of sports. He also likes going out and competing in his favourites sports. 


#### Project

My project consists mostly in creating a model to estimate the hydrogen amount in every section of steel billets and rods. With the increasing requirement of understanding how the hydrogen behaves in steel this project earn relevance because it allows to estimate the amount of hydrogen in each stage of the steelmaking and at every position, thing that no one has never been able to do before. Also, if you know the amount of hydrogenin a steel you can predict, if it is going to be affected with hydrogen embrittlement, that is one of the main problem of repurposing oil pipelines.
